title: ARSIA State Entry
description: A StateEntry is the fundamental unit of state in the ARSIA Protocol. It carries stored data, metadata, and compliance context. Every state operation (ARSIA-State.md §3) reads, writes, or queries StateEntry objects. Defined in ARSIA-State.md §2.1. Note: the serialized value MUST NOT exceed 1 MiB (1,048,576 bytes); this constraint is not expressible in JSON Schema and MUST be enforced programmatically — implementations MUST reject SET operations where the serialized value exceeds this limit with error code 'payload_too_large'.

key.description: Namespaced key in the format {agent-id}/{scope}/{local-key}. Globally unique identifier for a state entry within a deployment. The agent-id prefix MUST match the 'from' field of the SET request; the scope segment MUST match the entry's scope field. Per ARSIA-State.md §2.1.1.

value.description: The stored data. Any valid JSON value (object, array, string, number, boolean, or null). Opaque to the ARSIA protocol — the protocol does not interpret, validate, or transform the value. Maximum serialized size 1 MiB (enforced programmatically, not by this schema). Per ARSIA-State.md §2.1.2, §2.3.

owner_agent_id.description: Agent identifier of the agent that created this entry. Immutable after creation — MUST NOT be changed by any operation, including SET updates. Ownership determines access control and compliance responsibility. Per ARSIA-State.md §2.1.3.

scope.description: The lifecycle, visibility, and compliance scope of the entry, as defined in ARSIA-State.md §1. MUST match the scope segment of the entry's key. Immutable after creation. Per ARSIA-State.md §2.1.4.

allOf.description: RFC 3339 timestamp with millisecond precision and UTC designator, set by the implementation at creation time. Immutable thereafter. Baseline for retention period calculation (§4.1). Per ARSIA-State.md §2.1.5.
RFC 3339 timestamp with millisecond precision and UTC designator. Timestamp of the most recent modification. For newly created entries, equals created_at. Per ARSIA-State.md §2.1.6.

Explicit expiry timestamp for this entry. After this timestamp, the entry MAY be garbage-collected, but only once any effective retention period from compliance profile or retention_days has also elapsed. Per ARSIA-State.md §2.1.7.

retention_days.description: Explicit retention period in days for this specific entry, overriding the compliance profile's default retention. Effective retention is the maximum of entry.retention_days and the profile's retention — setting this field can EXTEND retention beyond the profile minimum but MUST NOT REDUCE it below the profile minimum. Per ARSIA-State.md §2.1.8.

allOf.description: Data residency zone for this entry. When pii_classification is 'personal', data_residency MUST be set either on this entry or inherited from the compliance profile. This cross-object invariant is enforced at runtime, not by this schema.

pii_classification.description: GDPR classification of the data in this entry. 'none': no personal data. 'pseudonymised': personal data pseudonymised per GDPR Art. 4(5) — still subject to GDPR obligations. 'personal': directly identifies a natural person — triggers the full GDPR obligation set. 'sensitive': special category data per GDPR Art. 9(1) — all 'personal' obligations apply, plus Art. 9(2) legal basis required, pii_special_categories required, and stricter access control. Immutable within a single version. Per ARSIA-State.md §2.1.10.

pii_special_categories.description: GDPR Art. 9(1) special category types. REQUIRED when pii_classification is 'sensitive'. MUST NOT be present otherwise. Per ARSIA-State.md §2.1.11.

version.description: Monotonically increasing version number. Set to 1 on creation and incremented by 1 on every successful SET that modifies the entry. Used with expected_version for optimistic concurrency control. Per ARSIA-State.md §2.1.12.

deleted.description: When true, the entry has been logically deleted via DELETE (§3.1). Logically deleted entries are not returned by GET or QUERY but MAY be returned by SNAPSHOT. Set by the implementation; MUST NOT be set directly by agents. Per ARSIA-State.md §2.1.13.
